assessment: Predicting if a tumour has aggressive or metastatic characteristics would be of great utility in the clinic as it would help patient management. In this manuscript, Carrier and collaborators derive a signature for melanoma aggressiveness relying on methylated regions of tumour and cell line genomes. The approach the authors take is innovative as it relies on the premise that genes that make cells be more aggressive should be detected across different organisms. In their results, the authors devise a DNA methylation score that correlates with survival and can be potentially useful for patient stratification.
